title: Euler-product form of the trace formula
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ and let $K$ be a Weil complex with
coefficients in $\Lambda$ satisfying the hypotheses of
[thm-trf-trace-formula-e] (if $\Lambda=E$) or of
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] (if $\Lambda=\Qlb$). These are
only the finite-level hypotheses (explicit etale-origin witnesses and
compactification admissibility for the reductions of a lattice of an
$E$-representative $K_E$). The Weil map $\varphi_E$ of $K_E$ is an
isomorphism of $D^b_c(X,E)$, but it need not be integral, or invertible
on any lattice after any rescaling. Write
$F=F^{\,1}_{c,K}$ for the global geometric Frobenius on
$H_c^i(X,K)$, and for a closed point $x\in|X_0|$ of degree
$e_x=[\kappa(x):\Fq]$ write $F_x$ for the one-circuit local Frobenius
on the stalk $K_{\bar x}$ (well defined up to conjugation). Put

$$
\det\bigl(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)
:=\prod_{j\in\mathbf Z}
\det\bigl(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid H^j(K_{\bar x})\bigr)^{(-1)^j},
\qquad
L(X_0,K,T)=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}
\det\bigl(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)^{-1}.
$$

Then:

1. The product defining $L(X_0,K,T)$ is locally finite for the
$T$-adic topology, and $L(X_0,K,T)\in1+T\Lambda[[T]]$.
1. As formal power series in $\Lambda[[T]]$,
$$
L(X_0,K,T)=\prod_{i\in\mathbf Z}
\det\bigl(1-TF\mid H_c^i(X,K)\bigr)^{(-1)^{i+1}},
$$
the product being finite.
1. If $\dim X_0\leq1$ and $K$ is a sheaf placed in degree zero, then
$H_c^i(X,K)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$, so the product in (2) runs
over $0\leq i\leq2$:
$$
L(X_0,K,T)=
\frac{\det(1-TF\mid H_c^1(X,K))}
{\det(1-TF\mid H_c^0(X,K))\,\det(1-TF\mid H_c^2(X,K))}.
$$
1. For every field embedding $\iota:\Qlb\to\mathbf C$, applying
$\iota$ coefficientwise carries the identity (2) (for $\Lambda=\Qlb$)
to the corresponding identity in $\mathbf C[[T]]$.

proof.text: For a finite-dimensional vector space over the characteristic-zero field $E$, [lem-weil-exp-trace-determinant] gives $\det(1-TG)^{-1}=\exp(\sum_{r\ge1}\operatorname{Tr}(G^r)T^r/r)$ for every endomorphism $G$. Over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [lem-zl-euler-product-identity] gives the same formula for the cohomological Frobenius modules constructed in Step 2. This is the logarithmic-determinant route of blueprint Step 0; no integral Weil structure is required. For a finite graded family, put $S_i=\sum_{r\ge1}\operatorname{Tr}(G_i^r)T^r/r$. The finite-sum identity of [lem-weil-power-series-exp-hom] gives $\exp(\sum_i(-1)^iS_i)=\prod_i\exp(S_i)^{(-1)^i}=\prod_i\det(1-TG_i)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$; the negative signs use $\exp(S_i)\exp(-S_i)=\exp(0)=1$. Substituting $T^e$ for $T$ gives the local identity with $T^{er}$. For an infinite family whose terms have orders tending to infinity, the same identity holds coefficientwise: by [def-weil-power-series-exponential], the coefficient of $T^N$ in $\exp(U)$ depends only on $U$ modulo $T^{N+1}$, so the finite-sum identity passes to the $T$-adic limit.

Apply [lem-trf-rational-global-frobenius-powers] to the chosen $E$-representative and its finite-level lattice. It identifies the specified operators with $F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=(F_{c,K_E}^{\,1})^m$. The scalar-extension assertion of [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] gives the same identity over $\Qlb$.

Apply [lem-trf-rational-local-frobenius-powers] to the invertible rational Weil map. For a degree-$e_x$ closed point it identifies every normalized lift operator $F_{y,m}$, for $e_x\mid m$, with $F_x^{m/e_x}$ up to conjugacy of stalk complexes. In particular $F_x$ is well defined up to conjugacy. Extending the displayed intertwining equality by the scalar extension of [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] proves the same statements over $\Qlb$.

Finally [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] and [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] give bounded finite-dimensional compact cohomology and stalk cohomology. Thus each inverse local determinant lies in $1+T^{e_x}\Lambda[[T]]$, while the global determinant product is finite.

For each $r\ge1$, [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] makes $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^r})$ finite. The geometric orbit assertion (1) of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy] gives exactly $e_x$ lifts of a degree-$e_x$ closed point in $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^{e_x}})$. Consequently the closed points of degree at most $N$ are images of the finite union of these rational-point sets for $1\le r\le N$. Each $e_x$ is positive, so no factor contributes below degree $e_x$ and only finitely many contribute through degree $N$. The Euler product therefore converges coefficientwise, and $T$-adically, in $1+T\Lambda[[T]]$. This proves clause (1) and justifies every rearrangement below. For $N=0$ all factors are $1$ modulo $T$.

Fix $m\ge1$. By the orbit assertion (1) of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy], a closed point $x$ has rational lifts in $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ exactly when $e_x\mid m$, with $e_x$ lifts in that case: on its cyclic orbit of length $e_x$, $g^m$ fixes every point precisely when $e_x\mid m$. The calculation in Step 3 of this split gives $F_{y,m}$ conjugate to $F_x^{m/e_x}$ on each lift. Conjugacy induces conjugacy on every cohomology space, hence equality of their ordinary traces (also [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], clauses (1) and (4)). Therefore [thm-trf-trace-formula-e], or [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar], gives
$$\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(F^m\mid H_c^i(X,K))=\sum_{e_x\mid m}e_x\,t_x(m/e_x),\qquad t_x(r)=\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^r\mid H^j(K_{\bar x})).$$

Multiply the trace identity of Step 6 by $T^m/m$ and sum over $m\ge1$. Reindexing $m=e_xr$ gives
$$\sum_{m\ge1}\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(F^m\mid H_c^i(X,K))T^m/m=\sum_x\sum_{r\ge1}t_x(r)T^{e_xr}/r,$$
since $e_x/m=1/r$. Step 5 makes this reindexing finite in every coefficient. Apply the formal exponential to both sides. The finite alternating determinant identity established in Step 1 identifies the left-hand side after exponentiating with the finite alternating cohomological determinant product. On the right, [lem-weil-power-series-exp-hom] and the coefficient formula of [def-weil-power-series-exponential] (Step 1) allow exponentiation through the locally finite sum; the determinant identity with $T^{e_x}$ in place of $T$ identifies the $x$-factor with $\det(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x})^{-1}$. This proves clause (2) directly, without requiring an uncited logarithm theorem.

Assume $\dim X_0\le1$ and $K$ is a sheaf in degree zero. If $\Lambda=E$ put $L=E$ and $K_L=K_E$. If $\Lambda=\Qlb$ with representative $(E,K_E)$, clause (3) of [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] makes $K$ isomorphic in the common-stage category to some $(L_1,N_1)$ with $N_1\in D^{\le0}_c$ and some $(L_2,N_2)$ with $N_2\in D^{\ge0}_c$; choose a finite $L\supseteq E,L_1,L_2$ over which both isomorphisms are represented. The truncations of [prop-constructible-truncations] commute with finite scalar extension, so $K_L=K_E\otimes_EL$ is a sheaf in degree zero in $D^b_c(X,L)$. Apply [lem-trf-curve-integral-lattice] over $L$ to $K_L$ with the lattice $K_L$ itself and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$; it needs no finite-level hypothesis, so nothing has to be transferred from the given lattice of $K_E$ to the larger field. From now on write $E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi,A_n$ for $L,\mathcal O_L,\varpi_L,\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^n$. The lemma supplies the torsion-free sheaf $M$, its normalized reductions $M_n$ with explicit etale-origin witnesses, and a bounded finite-free model $P=R\Gamma_c(X,M)$ with $P\otimes^LA_1\simeq R\Gamma_c(X,M_1)$ and $H_c^i(X,K_L)\simeq H^i(P)\otimes E$.

source.place: Step 5, curves: lattice, reduction tower and finite-free realization

proof.text: Choose a compactification of $X_0/k_0$ by [thm-nagata-compactification], replace the ambient scheme by the scheme-theoretic closure of $X_0$, and base change to $k$. This gives $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ with $\bar X$ proper of finite type over $k$. [lem-kun-dimension-extension] gives $\dim\bar X\le1$: first use equality of dimensions for the dense open $X_0$, then invariance under the field extension $k/k_0$.

source.place: Step 5, curves: Nagata compactification and the dimension bound

proof.text: The lattice lemma gives an explicit etale-origin witness for $M_1$, so [lem-trf-compactification-cohomology] identifies $P\otimes^LA_1\simeq R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!M_1)$. The sheaf $j_!M_1$ is constructible: use the strata of $M_1$ and the complementary closed stratum with value zero. By [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] it comes from a constructible etale $A_1$-sheaf; $A_1$ is a discrete finite field, hence noetherian. [sk-prop-sf-comparison] identifies its pro-etale and etale cohomology. Since $k$ is separably closed, [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] gives $c=0$, and [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] on the finite-type $k$-scheme $\bar X$ gives the bound $2\dim\bar X+c\le2$. Thus $H^i(P/\varpi P)=0$ for $i>2$; it also vanishes for $i<0$, because $j_!M_1$ is a sheaf in degree zero. Derived reduction is the termwise quotient here because $P$ is finite free.

source.place: Step 5, curves: finite-coefficient comparison and torsion-cohomological-dimension bound

proof.text: The short exact sequence of complexes $0\to P\xrightarrow{\varpi}P\to P/\varpi P\to0$ gives an injection $H^i(P)/\varpi H^i(P)\hookrightarrow H^i(P/\varpi P)$. For $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$ the target vanishes by Step 10. The module $H^i(P)$ is finitely generated over the noetherian DVR $\mathcal O_L$, so [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] applied to its maximal ideal $(\varpi_L)$ gives $H^i(P)=0$. Step 8 then gives $H_c^i(X,K_L)=0$ for these $i$; for $\Lambda=E$ this is the vanishing in clause (3). For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, [lem-weil-compact-support-finite-field-independence], applied to $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the representing isomorphisms $(E,K_E)\cong K\cong(L,K_L)$, identifies $R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)\otimes_E\Qlb$ with $R\Gamma_c(X,K_L)\otimes_L\Qlb$; cohomology commutes with these field extensions, so $H_c^i(X,K)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$, where $H_c^i(X,K)$ and $F$ are as in [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar]. Keeping degrees $0,1,2$ in clause (2) gives the displayed fraction, proving clause (3).

source.place: Step 5, curves: universal coefficient injection and Nakayama

proof.text: A field embedding iota:Q̄_l→C is a ring homomorphism. Its coefficientwise extension to formal power series preserves addition and multiplication coefficient by coefficient, inverses of series with constant term 1, and determinants because determinants are finite sums of products. Each coefficient of the locally finite Euler product is computed from finitely many factors, so applying iota to clause (2) gives the corresponding identity in C[[T]].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NL-3c019f806 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, all 12 steps, the 3 new nodes, the statement of every cited node, blueprint main-20261015 thm-trf-l-function-euler-product (statement and proof Steps 0-6; the statement is identical to master and to the node, not weakened), the unit sk-thm-trace-transport and the chapter. No SGA source is used. Coefficient categories are the rationalized E-stage and common-stage Q̄ℓ categories, with base-change transports rationalized via prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport. Steps 1-7, 9, 10 and 12 check out: exp/det signs; X_0(F_{q^m}) is finite by the finite coproduct in thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points; only the geometric clause (1) of the conjugacy lemma is used; reindexing m=e_x r is finite in each coefficient; Nagata closure and dimension invariance hold; the étale-origin witness gives compactification, then étale comparison, then cd ≤ 2d+0 ≤ 2. New nodes: the global powers node (B_{m+1}=B_{1,G^m}∘B_m in the orientation of def-trf-frobenius-operators; diag(1,ℓ) and φ=0 tested), the local powers node (cyclic transports with the source reparametrization; e=1, e=2 and noncommuting A_0,A_1 tested) and the lattice node (M=H^0/torsion; torsion lattices tested). All three are true, statement-only, not duplicates (lem-trf-global-frobenius-iterate-formula, lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition, lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy, lem-trf-frobenius-degree-formula, lem-trf-lattice-reduction-tower-normalized, lem-weil-pbc-lisse-e-constructible-integral-lattice compared) and not restated clauses of the item. Two repairable faults, both in the Q̄ℓ case of clause (3), repaired in fixes/. (1) E1: Step 8 must enlarge E to L, since the Q̄ℓ heart is defined at a larger stage (def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure (3)). It then applied lem-trf-curve-integral-lattice, which required a lattice with the finite-level hypotheses, and those hold only over O_E with no cited transfer to O_L. The lattice lemma never uses those hypotheses or the Weil structure: witnesses come from constructibility, and perfectness from prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems (1),(2). The repair removes both hypotheses from the new node, which makes it stronger and still true, and rewrites Step 8 to apply the lemma to K_L with lattice K_L. (2) C1/C4: Step 11 moved the vanishing from K_L back to the given representative using thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar, which does not state stage independence of RΓ_c. The repair cites the on-route reviewed lem-weil-compact-support-finite-field-independence (no cycle). proof_deps is updated.
